title: Using Analytical Performance/Power Model and Fine-Grained DVFS to Enhance AI Accelerator Energy Efficiency
problem: DVFS on AI processors has historically been applied at coarse granularity (entire program or sub-phases) because the control latency of DVFS mechanisms exceeds the duration of individual AI operators, leaving per-operator energy optimization unexploited. This coarse-grained DVFS fails to match voltage/frequency to the actual compute intensity of each AI operator.
motivation: Deep learning workloads are driving rapidly increasing AI processor energy consumption, making fine-grained power optimization critical to sustaining AI development within power budgets.
method: Most voltage/frequency scaling happens at the program level because the switching overhead exceeds individual operation duration. But operations have different needs: memory-bound operations (waiting for data) and compute-bound operations (needing raw speed) benefit from different settings. The paper uses an analytical model to predict each operation's type, plus a hardware mechanism to reduce switching overhead, enabling per-operation voltage/frequency scaling: memory-bound operations run slower (saving energy during waits) and compute-bound operations run at full speed.
key_novelty: An analytical model predicts the energy-speed trade-off for each AI operation (how much slower it gets if you run at lower voltage/frequency), enabling per-operation voltage/frequency scaling without hardware profiling.
contributions: Analytical performance/power model characterizing compute- vs. memory-boundedness of AI operators
Fine-grained DVFS control mechanism at AI-operator granularity overcoming DVFS latency constraints
Energy efficiency improvement for AI accelerators demonstrated across deep learning workloads

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: energy efficiency improvement (specific numbers not in abstract)

limitations: Detailed energy savings numbers and hardware overhead of the fine-grained DVFS control mechanism are not stated in the abstract.
primary_theme: fine-grained DVFS for AI accelerator energy efficiency
